@[[1b8b4fd9-6c8c-4a83-b20e-d1a52e8b4f08]] Stage 2 handoff part 3/7: applicable Stage 1 specification, sections 7–9.

## 7 Idempotency
POST /reservations and POST /reservation-moves require Idempotency-Key 1..255, scoped per authenticated user. Same key/body on different path is a distinct request. Resolve after JSON object parsing and authentication, before endpoint validation/resource checks. Same key different JSON body -> 409 even if body invalid. Missing/empty -> 400; first successful use 201; same key/body/method/path replay -> 200 with original JSON value; different body -> 409; failed 4xx doesn't consume key. JSON key order/whitespace irrelevant. Concurrent identical unused key: one 201, rest 200, one effect. Replay returns original after resource changes/cancel and causes no mutation.

## 8 API
Public GET /restaurants -> {"restaurants":[{id,name,timezone}]}; GET /restaurants/{id} returns fixture shape including slot_minutes,duration,cutoff,opening_hours,tables (unknown 404); GET /availability requires restaurant_id,date,party_size (missing 422), date is local calendar date. Returns restaurant/date/timezone and slots with starts_at_local, offset starts_at, available_table_ids. Include every slot_minutes step where slot+duration<=close; table IDs fixture order for enough capacity and no confirmed overlap. Occupied slots still appear empty; closed day [].
POST /reservations idempotent, body restaurant_id/table_id/starts_at_local/party_size. Local timestamp no offset, resolve restaurant zone. 201 response has reservation_id, immutable globally unique 6..12 A-Z0-9 reference, restaurant_id,table_id,party_size,confirmed status,local start, offset start/end,created_at. Overlap 409 table_unavailable; off-grid 422 not_on_slot_grid; outside hours/end after close 422 outside_opening_hours; over capacity 422 party_exceeds_capacity; invalid party 422 validation_failed; nonexistent local time 422 invalid_local_time; unknown/foreign table/restaurant 404.
GET /reservations returns caller's confirmed and cancelled, starts_at descending, same shape; empty [].
GET /reservations/{reference}: caller only, other owner 404.
POST /reservations/{reference}/cancel -> 200 current state; repeat 200; cutoff or later 409 cutoff_passed; not own 404; frees slot.
PATCH /reservations/{reference}: any subset table_id,starts_at_local,party_size; no idempotency. Create validation; cutoff against current start; cancelled 409 reservation_cancelled. Success atomic, failure unchanged. Reference/id survive.

## 9 Time and DST
Zone-local time. Spring skipped local times absent/unbookable -> 422 invalid_local_time. Fall repeated time resolves only first occurrence and appears once. Duration is absolute elapsed time; a 90-minute booking from fall-back 01:30 can end locally 02:00. Handle Berlin 2026-03-29 and 2026-10-25, New York 2026-03-08 and 2026-11-01 with IANA offsets.

## 10 Export/import
Unauthenticated GET /_test/export and POST /_test/import. Export 200 {track:"tablekeeper",format_version:1,state:implementation-defined}; import accepts unchanged export, atomically replaces destination state and returns 204. No dependence on source process/files/volume/port/network. Repeated import restores without duplication. Invalid JSON per §5; missing fields/wrong track/version/invalid state -> 422 without destination changes. 10s control timeout. Export is atomic read-only snapshot, not mutated by later writes.
Preserve accounts/password hashes and login, existing bearer tokens, fixture config, reservations/references, every successful idempotent request body and original response. Do not regenerate identities/status/timestamps. Failed keys reusable. Existing receipts/references/tokens/retries survive import; importing fresh fixture doesn't satisfy. Import removes all old destination data/credentials; reset clears imported state too. State needn't survive abrupt restart.

## 11 Atomic reservation moves
Authenticated POST /reservation-moves requires idempotency. moves 1..8 distinct string references; malformed/duplicate -> 422. All own and same restaurant; unknown/other owner ->404; different restaurants ->422; no token ->401.
Each item accepts PATCH fields table_id,starts_at_local,party_size; omitted retains; unknown ignored. Identity/owner/created_at immutable. Cancelled ->409 reservation_cancelled. Existing cutoff applies. Non-occupancy errors follow ordinary amend codes, in input order; cutoff precedes other changes on each item. Result overlap with any resulting or unlisted booking ->409 table_unavailable. Unchanged listed bookings retain occupancy.
Atomic all-or-nothing including occupancy/records/retry keys. Success 201 {"reservations":[...]} in input order including unchanged. Replay original response with 200 after later amendment/cancel. No-op retains all values. Export/import preserves successful batch receipts and resulting bookings. No UI required.

{"args":{"body":"@christianelena92/chris-builder Stage 2 handoff part 5/7: complete Stage 2 official specification, sections beginning through signup/login and search.

# Tablekeeper — Stage 2: online booking and combined tables
Stage 1 requirements continue to apply; numbered references point to stage-1.md. Diners search/book/manage reservations in a browser; restaurants may offer approved table pairs for large parties. Required routes reachable directly: / search+availability grid, /signup, /login, /lookup. These return HTML; API JSON convention doesn't apply.

## Competing clients and uncertain outcomes
Handle out-of-order responses and post-submit connection failures. If search A starts before B but ends after it, grid/table labels/form must describe B; late A cannot restore results. If a table is taken by another client after form open, 409 table_unavailable displays booking-error and refreshes availability while preserving form and inputs; no confirmation. If booking response is lost, even after commit, show nonempty booking-uncertain, not booking-error or confirmation. Unchanged form retries same idempotency key/body. Successful retry clears uncertainty/error and shows original reference; confirmed rejection uses booking-error. Applies to combinations. No polling/live updates/cross-tab sync/reload recovery. Server is authoritative; never synthesize success from cache.
Expose required data-testid attributes below. Additional elements allowed; visual implementation is team choice subject to product direction.

## Product and visual direction
Coherent presentation-ready restaurant product, warm confident hospitality character, clear hierarchy; easy to scan dates/times/party/table choices. Combinations should read as seating options, not identifiers. Consistent typography/spacing/color/controls/feedback. Primary actions obvious. Available/unavailable/selected/loading/success/refused/uncertain states visually distinct. Prominent human labels; technical IDs only when helpful. Usable at 375 CSS px and desktop without horizontal scroll. Visible labels, keyboard focus, sufficient contrast, considered empty/loading/error states, consistent navigation. Custom art/reference match not required.

# Tablekeeper — Stage 2: online booking and combined tables
Stage 1 requirements continue to apply; numbered references point to stage-1.md. Diners search/book/manage reservations in a browser; restaurants may offer approved table pairs for large parties. Required routes reachable directly: / search+availability grid, /signup, /login, /lookup. These return HTML; API JSON convention doesn't apply.

## Competing clients and uncertain outcomes
Handle out-of-order responses and post-submit connection failures. If search A starts before B but ends after it, grid/table labels/form must describe B; late A cannot restore results. If a table is taken by another client after form open, 409 table_unavailable displays booking-error and refreshes availability while preserving form and inputs; no confirmation. If booking response is lost, even after commit, show nonempty booking-uncertain, not booking-error or confirmation. Unchanged form retries same idempotency key/body. Successful retry clears uncertainty/error and shows original reference; confirmed rejection uses booking-error. Applies to combinations. No polling/live updates/cross-tab sync/reload recovery. Server is authoritative; never synthesize success from cache.
Expose required data-testid attributes below. Additional elements allowed; visual implementation is team choice subject to product direction.

## Product and visual direction
Coherent presentation-ready restaurant product, warm confident hospitality character, clear hierarchy; easy to scan dates/times/party/table choices. Combinations should read as seating options, not identifiers. Consistent typography/spacing/color/controls/feedback. Primary actions obvious. Available/unavailable/selected/loading/success/refused/uncertain states visually distinct. Prominent human labels; technical IDs only when helpful. Usable at 375 CSS px and desktop without horizontal scroll. Visible labels, keyboard focus, sufficient contrast, considered empty/loading/error states, consistent navigation. Custom art/reference match not required.

docker build -t tablekeeper-stage-1 .

The service listens on `0.0.0.0` and stores all state in its container-local SQLite database. It uses only Python's standard library at runtime.

{"is_error":false,"name":"Bash","output":"# Tablekeeper — Stage 2: online booking and combined tables

The stage-1 requirements continue to apply, with the additions below. Numbered section
references such as §5 and §7 refer to `stage-1.md`.

Diners can search, book and manage reservations in a browser. Restaurants can offer
approved pairs of tables for larger parties.

The following screens must be reachable by URL. Other screens must be reachable through
the UI. Server-side and client-side rendering are both permitted.

| Route | Screen |
|---|---|
| `/` | Search and availability grid |
| `/signup` | Signup |
| `/login` | Login |
| `/lookup` | Look up a reservation by reference |

A screen route returns HTML; §3.4's `application/json` convention is about the API, and does
not govern the routes in the table above.

## Competing clients and uncertain outcomes

The UI must handle responses arriving out of order and connections failing after submission.

- If search A starts before search B but finishes after it, the grid, table labels and
  booking form must describe B. A late response must not restore A's results.
- If another client takes a table after the form opens, a `409 table_unavailable` response
  shows `booking-error` and refreshes availability. Preserve the selected form and its
  inputs so the diner can change their choice. Do not show a confirmation for that attempt.
- If a booking response is lost, including after the booking commits, show nonempty
  `booking-uncertain` text, without `booking-error` or a new confirmation. The unchanged
  form must retry with the same idempotency key and body. A successful retry removes the
  uncertainty/error elements and shows the original reference. A confirmed rejection
  uses `booking-error`.

These rules apply to combination bookings too. No background polling, live updates,
cross-tab storage synchronization, or recovery across a page reload is required. The server
remains authoritative; the browser must not manufacture a successful result from cached data.

The UI must expose the `data-testid` attributes listed below for integration testing.
Additional elements are permitted, and the visual implementation is the team's choice subject
to the product-quality requirements below.

## Product and visual direction

The browser experience must feel like a coherent, presentation-ready restaurant product, not a
test harness with controls attached. Aim for a warm, confident hospitality character. The search,
availability and booking flow should have an obvious visual hierarchy; a diner should be able to
scan dates, times, party size and table choices without having to interpret raw API data. Combined
tables should read as intentional seating options, not as concatenated technical identifiers.

Use a consistent visual system for typography, spacing, colour, controls and feedback. Primary
actions must be easy to identify. Available, unavailable, selected, loading, successful, refused
and uncertain states must be visually distinct as well as satisfying the behavioural requirements
below. Use human-readable restaurant and table labels prominently; expose technical identifiers
only where they help the user.

The required flows must remain clear and usable at a 375 CSS-pixel viewport and at conventional
desktop widths, without horizontal page scrolling. Inputs need visible labels, keyboard focus must
be apparent, and text and controls need sufficient contrast. Provide considered empty, loading and
error states, and keep navigation consistent across the required routes. A custom illustration,
brand asset or exact visual match to a reference is not required.

## Signup and login

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `signup-email`, `signup-password`, `signup-display-name` | Inputs |
| `signup-submit` | Button |
| `login-email`, `login-password`, `login-submit` | Inputs and button |
| `auth-error` | Error message. Present only when there is one |
| `current-user` | Visible on every screen when signed in. Text contains the display name |
| `logout-button` | Button |

@[[6409fcfb-2fb9-4c93-9968-58213828f0c2]] Stage 2 review handoff part 6/7. Complete Stage 2 spec—search, booking, lookup, upgrades, combinations:

## Search / grid
On /: restaurant-select (option values restaurant IDs), date-input YYYY-MM-DD, party-size-input number, search-button, availability-grid, slot-{table_id}-{HH:MM} per table/slot, no-slots instead of grid if none. Each cell has data-available true exactly if table ID is in availability.available_table_ids for searched party size; else false. Available click opens booking form for table/slot; unavailable no action. Signed out shows auth-error or navigates login.

## Booking & confirmation
booking-form, booking-summary includes table label/local time, booking-party-size prefilled, booking-submit, booking-error on failure. Keep form after success. Submitting unchanged again returns same confirmation-reference, no error/duplicate. Changing field creates new booking request; use §7 retries. Confirmation IDs: confirmation container, confirmation-reference exact reference only, confirmation-details includes restaurant/table/local time.

## Lookup /lookup
lookup-reference-input and lookup-submit. reservation-detail when found; reservation-status exactly confirmed/cancelled; reservation-cancel-button absent after cancel; reservation-error for not found/refused cancel.

## Existing clients after upgrade
Stage 2 accepts export from team's Stage 1. Browser signed in before export/import remains signed in after. Retained ref works in lookup. Booking response lost before export remains retryable after import with same body/key and UI recovers original confirmation. Import may occur between browser requests; no need in-flight migration/reload/new screen. Form and pending retry identity persist.

## Combined table model/API
Restaurant fixture adds combinable: unordered pairs only, e.g. [["t_1","t_2"],["t_2","t_3"]]. Never >2; unlisted pair forbidden regardless of capacity; nontransitive. Pair capacity is sum. Seeded reservations default confirmed unless status cancelled; may carry table_id or table_ids.
GET /availability adds available_options; available_table_ids stays singles. Options include all available singles and declared pairs with enough summed capacity and no overlap on any member; singles first fixture order, pairs afterward combinable order; pair table_ids preserve combinable order.
POST /reservations body uses table_ids; table_id remains accepted as singleton. Both sent ->422 validation_failed. Responses always table_ids, plus table_id iff set has one member. Unlisted pair or >2 ->422 combination_not_allowed; overlap on any member ->409 table_unavailable; party>sum capacity ->422 party_exceeds_capacity; duplicate IDs ->422. PATCH /reservations/{ref} accepts table_ids same rules. Cancel frees every member.

def test_submitting_the_booking_form_twice_books_once(seeded, page):
    """The form stays on screen, so a second press sends the same body. A form
    that mints its idempotency key at submit time sends a new one and is answered
    409 table_unavailable."""
    _open_booking_form(page)
    page.click(sel("booking-submit"))
    page.wait_for_selector(sel("confirmation"))
    first = page.text_content(sel("confirmation-reference")).strip()

    page.click(sel("booking-submit"))
    page.wait_for_timeout(500)
    assert page.query_selector(sel("booking-error")) is None, \
        "the second submit was refused instead of replayed"
    assert page.text_content(sel("confirmation-reference")).strip() == first


def test_a_double_submit_leaves_one_reservation(seeded, page, api):
    _open_booking_form(page)
    page.click(sel("booking-submit"))
    page.wait_for_selector(sel("confirmation"))
    page.click(sel("booking-submit"))
    page.wait_for_timeout(500)

    ada = api().authenticate(fx.ADA["email"], fx.ADA["password"])
    confirmed = [r for r in ada.get("/reservations").json()["reservations"]
                 if r["status"] == "confirmed"]
    assert len(confirmed) == 1, f"booked {len(confirmed)} times"


def test_changing_the_form_first_is_a_different_booking(seeded, page, api):
    """Editing a field starts a new booking, so it must not replay the old one."""
    _open_booking_form(page)
    page.click(sel("booking-submit"))
    page.wait_for_selector(sel("confirmation"))
    page.fill(sel("booking-party-size"), "2")
    page.click(sel("booking-submit"))
    page.wait_for_timeout(500)
    assert page.query_selector(sel("booking-error")) is not None, \
        "the slot is taken, so a genuinely new booking of it must be refused"
